taskDescription: Click every word in the passage that names a protein encoded by the HIV genome. For a two-word name, click both words.
textField: HIV attaches to host cells using *gp120*, which binds the CD4 receptor, and *gp41*, which drives membrane fusion. The *p24* capsid encloses two copies of the RNA genome and three viral enzymes. *Reverse* *transcriptase* copies RNA into DNA, *integrase* inserts the proviral DNA into the host chromosome, and *protease* cleaves the *Gag-Pol* polyprotein so that new virions can mature.

overallFeedback.feedback: gp120 (CD4 binding), gp41 (membrane fusion), p24 (capsid protein used in rapid diagnostic assays), reverse transcriptase (copies RNA into DNA, target of NRTIs/NNRTIs), integrase (proviral insertion, target of dolutegravir), protease (polyprotein cleavage, target of ritonavir) and Gag-Pol (the viral precursor polyprotein that protease cleaves) are all HIV-encoded proteins. CD4 is a host receptor, not a viral protein.
